title: Least Frequently Used Cache
statement:
Design a fixed-capacity key-value cache that evicts the least frequently used entry when full, breaking frequency ties by evicting the least recently used entry.

Contract
- `new Solution(capacity)` initializes a cache with capacity `capacity >= 0`.
- `get(key)` returns the value stored for `key` if present, or `-1` otherwise. Accessing a present key increments its use frequency by `1` and marks it most recently used within its new frequency tier.
- `put(key, value)` inserts or updates `key` with `value`:
  - If `capacity == 0`, `put` does nothing.
  - If `key` is already present, update its value, increment its frequency by `1`, and mark it most recently used in its new tier.
  - If `key` is new and the cache is at capacity, evict the key with the lowest frequency; if multiple keys share that minimum frequency, evict the least recently used among them. Insert the new key with frequency `1`.
- Both `get` and `put` must run in O(1) average time.

Examples
- Capacity `2`: `put(1, 10)`, `put(2, 20)`, `get(1)` -> `10`, `put(3, 30)` evicts `2`, `get(2)` -> `-1`, `get(3)` -> `30`.
- Tie-breaking: Capacity `2`, `put(1, 1)`, `put(2, 2)`, `put(3, 3)` evicts `1` (both `1` and `2` had frequency `1`, and `1` was older), so `get(1)` -> `-1` and `get(2)` -> `2`.
- Capacity `0`: `put(1, 1)`, `get(1)` -> `-1`.

examples.input: cap 2; put 1 10, put 2 20, get 1, put 3 30, get 2, get 3
cap 2; put 1 1, put 2 2, put 3 3, get 1, get 2

hints: Scanning all keys to find the minimum frequency takes O(capacity) per eviction. Instead, group keys by their frequency count.

Keep a map from key to (value, frequency) and a second map from frequency to an ordered bucket (a doubly linked list or LinkedHashSet) so adding, promoting, and evicting the oldest entry in a tier are all O(1).

Track minFreq: inserting a new key resets minFreq to 1; promoting a key from minFreq to minFreq + 1 increments minFreq when the minFreq bucket becomes empty. Intended complexity: O(1) average per operation (O(n) over n operations), O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: cap C; op1, op2, ... where ops are put k v | get k, for example: cap 2; put 1 10, put 2 20, get 1, put 3 30, get 2, get 3
